chunks: Ishaq said: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying:

I complained to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the constriction of imprisonment and the heaviness of the shackles. So he wrote to me: "Today you will pray the zuhr salat (prayer) in your home." Then I was brought out at the time of zuhr, and I performed it in my home just as he (peace be upon him) had said.

And I was under hardship, so I wanted to ask him for dinars in the letter, but I felt shy. Then when I came to my home, he sent to me one hundred dinars and wrote to me: "If you have a need, then do not be shy and do not hold back; ask for it, for you shall see what you love, if Allah so wills."

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the zuhr salat (prayer), the midday obligatory prayer
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: gold dinars, a form of money
key_terms.ضِيقَ الْحَبْسِ: the constriction and hardship of imprisonment
key_terms.فَلَا تَسْتَحْيِ: do not be shy in expressing your need
key_terms.كَتَلَ الْقَيْدِ: the heaviness or burden of shackles
key_terms.مُضَيَّقًا: being under constraint, especially financial hardship
key_terms.مِائَةِ دِينَارٍ: one hundred dinars sent as assistance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the knowledge and generosity of Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a report from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari about the foreknowledge and generosity of Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام). It describes his release from confinement in time to perform zuhr salat (prayer) at home, and the Imam's sending of financial assistance before being explicitly asked.

en.hubeali: Is’haq said, ‘Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary narrated to me saying,

‘I complained to Abu Muhammad of the constraint of the prison and the restraining blocks (shackles). So heasws wrote to me: ‘You will be praying Al-Zohr Salat in your own home today’. So I came out (from the prison) during the time of Al-Zohr Salat, and I prayed it in my own house just as heasws had said.

And I was (financially) constrained, so I wanted to seek Dinars from him<sup>asws</sup> in the letter, but I was too embarrassed. So when I went to my house, he<sup>asws</sup> diverted to me with one hundred Dinars and wrote to me: ‘Whenever there was a need for you, so neither be shy nor reserved, and seek it, for you will see what you love, if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ishaq has said that abu Hashim al-Ja‘fari has said the following.

“I complained to abu Muhammad (a.s.) about the constraining cell of the prison and the weight of the shackles on me. He wrote back in reply to me. “Today you will pray your noontime prayer in your own home.” I then was released that day and prayed the noontime prayer in my own home as he had said.”

I was under financial constrains and I decided to ask him for a certain amount of Dinars in writing but I felt shy. When was going to my home he sent me a hundred Dinars and had written to me this. “If you need anything do not feel shy or embarrassed. Ask and you will find it as you wanted, by the will of Allah.”
